title: Assurance
description: Evaluate a specific privacy, integrity, numeric, implementation, or deployment claim.
text: An assurance record identifies the exact plan, component versions, threat model, protected values, visible information, corruption and collusion assumptions, numeric policy, environment, procedure, result, and limitations. Reference tests, formal analysis, cryptographic review, transport hardening, deployment inspection, and leakage tests answer different questions. Missing assurance is not a failed test, but it is not a pass. Evidence for participants that follow the protocol does not establish security against malicious behavior. A publication claim must cite the relevant records and keep their limitations. See reading research and evidence. Python SDK example from pllm import assure report = assure() print(report.schemaversion, report.todict()["limitations"]) Report scope is bundled assurance fixtures, not universal privacy proof.

title: Benchmarks
description: Measure PLLM systems with reproducible records and compare only equivalent runs.
text: pllm.benchmark(...) measures supported native compiled regions and returns an immutable EvidenceReport. pllm.deploymentbenchmark(request) validates observations supplied by the caller, but cannot prove where they came from. The CLI does not currently have a pllm benchmark command. Every record identifies whether it covers a compiled region, protocol, deployment, complete model, privacy test, or quality test. Compare runs only when the model, body fingerprint, plan, workload, numeric settings, environment, threads, SIMD settings, warmup, repetitions, and cold or warm mode match. The local dashboard helps diagnose a loopback deployment, but it does not create a canonical evidence record. See metrics and research experiments. Python SDK example from inspect import signature from pllm import benchmark print(signature(benchmark)) This shows required benchmark inputs without implying that an uncompiled model can run.

title: Command-line interface
description: Inspect PLLM configuration, components, and research records from the terminal.
text: The PLLM command-line interface inspects the package's public metadata. It does not currently start inference services, compile executable plans, or run benchmarks. Install the command uv tool install pllm pllm --help This installs the pllm wheel from PyPI in an isolated tool environment. Use uv tool upgrade pllm to update it. Available commands - pllm config validates and exports public configuration. - pllm components lists built-in component descriptions. - pllm research lists research sources, methods, and recipes or assesses a proposed publication record. - pllm dev contains development-only tools. Run pllm COMMAND --help for the options accepted by a command. Use --format json when another program will consume the result. Continue - CLI reference lists every current command and option. - SDK configuration explains configuration files and content identity. - Research methods explains the records returned by pllm research.

title: Compiler
description: Learn how PLLM turns a model plan and component choices into a checked execution plan.
text: Compilation combines a model plan, component choices, workload limits, and policy. It checks operator support, value formats, conversions, numeric settings, party placement, preparation, native kernels, and assurance requirements. The result is an executable plan with a content digest. The coverage report names every missing operator, conversion, party role, numeric bound, assurance record, or compatible component version. Required gaps stop compilation instead of triggering a hidden fallback. All model families use the same semantic model format. Current research profiles cannot execute a complete listed model plan. A model adapter can therefore be available while full private inference remains unsupported. Python SDK example import json from pathlib import Path from pllm import compile request = json.loads(Path("compile-request.json").readtext(encoding="utf-8")) plan = compile(request) print(plan.executionplandigest) Compilation rejects unsupported coverage rather than hiding it behind a fallback. Complete model compilation remains unsupported for current research profiles.

title: Add a category
description: Extend the semantic component graph when an existing category cannot express a real contract.
text: Add a category only when existing operator, representation, protocol, conversion, preparation, kernel, compiler, runtime, deployment, metric, search, or assurance contracts cannot express the new capability without ambiguity. Define ownership, descriptor schema, composition rules, lifecycle, validation, compatibility, evidence, public API, CLI discovery, generated reference, documentation, and migration policy together. Do not name a reusable category after one paper or model. Python SDK example from pllm.components import listcomponents categories = sorted({component.category for component in listcomponents()}) print(categories) Inspect existing categories before proposing a new contract.

title: Component standard
description: Required identity, lifecycle, representation, role, capability, evidence, and limitation fields.
text: 1. Choose a semantic category and stable authority-owned identity. 2. Define versioned parameters, lifecycle phase, input and output representations, host requirements, roles, artifacts, and evidence pointers. 3. Implement in the semantic owner, not a paper-named runtime path. 4. Add static discovery and identity tests without importing provider or native runtime code. 5. Add compatibility and operator-coverage tests. 6. Add runtime, benchmark, quality, assurance, and deployment evidence independently when each exists. The canonical contract is design/component-standard.md. Missing fields remain not recorded; empty evidence is not a pass. Python SDK example from pllm.components import getcomponent descriptor = getcomponent("pllm/cpu") print(descriptor.todict()) Built-in descriptors expose the public fields contributors must keep discoverable.

title: Contribute
description: Add a model, component, research method, or evidence record without creating a one-off runtime path.
text: Start with the component standard. Model families use shared operations, research methods transform plans, providers expose generic capabilities, and benchmark or assurance results attach to exact versions. Keep identity, implementation, coverage, evidence, quality, privacy, and deployment status separate. Do not add compiler branches named after a paper or hidden registration that exists only in one runtime. Python SDK example from pllm.components import listcomponents for component in listcomponents(): print(component.component, component.category, component.version) Contributors should preserve this side-effect-free discovery contract.

title: Native plugin ABI
description: Boundary requirements for future independently distributed native capability providers.
text: The installed native module is currently built with PLLM. A stable third-party native plugin ABI is not published. Any future ABI must version ownership, allocation, byte layout, alignment, panic isolation, threading, cancellation, capability negotiation, artifact identity, host-feature detection, and error translation. Python entry points must remain lightweight and side-effect-free during discovery. Python SDK example from pllm.kernels import Cpu print(Cpu.describe().distribution) This discovers the built-in distribution only. No third-party native plugin ABI is published.

title: Publish a provider
description: Expose a component implementation without importing it during core discovery.
text: A provider package publishes signed or digest-addressed descriptor metadata, implementation artifacts, host requirements, supported component versions, representations, roles, and evidence references. Discovery reads static metadata before any trusted code executes. Provider identity does not imply operator identity or trust. Loading requires explicit policy, compatibility validation, and artifact verification. Distribution, component, provider, deployment, and evidence versions remain separate. Python SDK example from pllm.components import getcomponent descriptor = getcomponent("pllm/masked-linear") print(descriptor.provider, descriptor.distribution, descriptor.artifacts) Discovery reads metadata only and does not load provider code.

title: Upstreaming
description: Move validated research work into maintained semantic and runtime components.
text: Upstreaming requires locked sources, a clean-room implementation record where applicable, fidelity tests, model-neutral semantics, component identity, compiler coverage, numeric analysis, matched benchmark evidence, scoped assurance, quality evaluation, limitations, and maintenance ownership. A new publication claim also needs a stable method ID and evidence that isolates the contribution from the baseline. Failed and negative results remain useful research records. Python SDK example from pllm.components import getcomponent component = getcomponent("pllm/kv-cache-eviction") print(component.version, component.evidence) Empty evidence remains not recorded; component presence alone is not an upstreaming claim.

title: Conversions
description: Learn how values move between numeric formats, layouts, and owners.
text: Conversions connect components that use different formats. Examples include a quantized tensor to ring values, arithmetic shares to bits, residues to signed integers, a packed matrix to row-major layout, or server shares to client output. Each conversion records bounds, rounding, network traffic, ownership, visible information, and assurance requirements. The compiler can insert only a declared conversion that satisfies both component interfaces. A matching Python or Rust type cannot silently open a private value or allow a lossy cast. Python SDK example from pllm.components import listcomponents conversions = [item for item in listcomponents() if "conversion" in item.category] print(conversions) An empty result means no built-in conversion component is currently published; it does not authorize an implicit cast.

title: Deployment
description: Learn how to assign PLLM roles to authenticated services without changing privacy assumptions.
text: A deployment assigns each protocol role to a process and operator. It records endpoints, authentication, separate credentials, provider identity, storage, capacity, expiration, observability, shutdown behavior, and trust boundaries. The client must keep plaintext prompts, masks, private scales, model state, and decoding. Client-to-inference, client-to-preparation, and preparation-to-inference connections use different credentials. Changing the URL of an ordinary model API does not make its unmodified SDK private. A loopback run checks that the services work together on one machine. It does not show that production operators are independent. Deployment assurance must refer to the exact plan and environment being evaluated. Python SDK example from pllm.deployment import Deployment deployment = Deployment.local(root=".pllm/local") print(deployment.tospec()) This creates configuration only. Generic remote role deployment is not supported.

title: Kernels
description: Understand PLLM's native integer matrix kernels, memory costs, and CPU requirements.
text: pllm-core implements bounded integer matrices, scalar reference code, runtime AVX2 and NEON selection, codecs, quantization, masking, subtraction, and operating system randomness. It copies validated weights into Rust once and reuses them. Python-to-Rust buffer conversions still create copies. Kernel records list required CPU features, threading, input and output formats, supported operations, memory use, and evidence. Moving arithmetic to Rust does not remove protocol messages, offline preparation, client state, or conversion costs. Python SDK example from pllm.kernels import Cpu kernel = Cpu(threads=4) print(kernel.tospec()) This selects public kernel configuration only; it does not execute a model.

title: Arithmetic and Boolean garbling
description: Compare arithmetic and Boolean garbling without treating one primitive as a complete private runtime.
text: Arithmetic garbling works with modular integer values. Boolean garbling works with bit-level circuits, often using half-gates and free-XOR-compatible labels. Lookup tables and weighted paths are ways to represent a computation; they do not provide identical protocol or security guarantees. Moving values between arithmetic and Boolean forms changes range, bit width, truncation, and communication requirements. A fast primitive does not make a complete transformer executable. Correct reference code is also not a substitute for cryptographic review. Read garbling protocols and conversions for the exact interfaces and current limits.

title: Learn
description: Understand PLLM's private inference runtime, research harness, trust assumptions, and evidence.
text: PLLM is a Rust-first, Python-friendly runtime and research harness for private large language model inference across multiple parties. Its goal is to let a client use remote compute without giving any one compute party the complete request, model state, and output. PLLM combines two systems: - The inference runtime assigns work to the client, preparation service, and inference service while preserving an explicit trust boundary. - The research harness turns papers and hypotheses into independent Rust and Python implementations, then records provenance, plans, tests, benchmarks, limitations, and publication review separately. PLLM is being built for high performance, but performance depends on the exact model, protocol, hardware, network, and workload. Privacy depends on the selected protocol, correct implementation, and stated non-collusion assumptions. Treat the project's economic and safety benefits as goals; use evidence records for measured results and current support for executable coverage. Start here if you need to decide whether a PLLM workflow matches your privacy, performance, or deployment requirements: 1. Privacy and threat models 2. Parties and offline work 3. Masked linear inference 4. Arithmetic and Boolean garbling 5. Numeric semantics and model quality 6. Reading research and evidence These pages explain the concepts. The reference section lists exact APIs and schemas. Current support reports which combinations are available.

title: Masked linear inference
description: Follow seeded one-time masks through offline correction and online matrix evaluation.
text: For public matrix W, preparation material binds a one-time input mask r, output mask s, and ticket. Preparation computes Wr-s and installs it at inference. Online, the client sends x-r; inference combines it with the correction and returns Wx-s; the client adds s. This changes timing, not algebra. Reusing a row reveals relations between activations, so each ticket is consumed once. The inference role must never receive the seed, and the preparation role must not retain masks or collude with inference. Prefill packs a ticket vector and masked matrix per stage. Decode uses one ticket per stage on a persistent connection. See masked-linear protocol for the component boundary.

title: Numeric semantics and model quality
description: Understand how integer arithmetic affects correctness and model output quality.
text: A model description defines the intended operators. An executable plan must also choose integer representations, quantization scales, ring widths, nonlinear approximations, and decoding rules. Each choice can introduce error or overflow. PLLM selects u16, u24, or u32 rings from the maximum signed output of each prepared stage. This prevents overflow in that stage. It does not show that a complete generation matches the source model. Quantized token lookup and output head behavior also depend on the bundle schema and matrix orientation. Report numeric error, overflow analysis, token agreement, and task quality as separate results. See numerics and representations.

title: Parties and offline work
description: Learn what each party does before and during a private inference request.
text: The client holds plaintext and authorizes each request. The preparation service creates one-time protocol material before a request. The inference service consumes that material while evaluating the model. A provider implements a component. An operator controls a deployed process and its policy. For public-weight inference, preparation commits to the model, transformer body, stages, quantization, and retry limit. It expands seeds supplied by the client into input masks, output masks, and one-time tickets. It computes corrections, sends them to inference, and waits for confirmation. During inference, only the client and inference service exchange tickets and masked activations. Reserved rows can be used only once. Cancellation, failure, replay, or early completion invalidates every unused row in that reservation. See preparation and deployment.

title: Privacy and threat models
description: Learn what PLLM protects, what each party can see, and which trust assumptions still apply.
text: To evaluate a private inference system, ask six questions: 1. Which values should remain private? 2. Which metadata can each party see? 3. Which parties must follow the protocol? 4. Which parties must not collude? 5. Who receives the output? 6. What evidence supports each answer? In PLLM's prepared public-weight path, prompts, decoded output, seeds, masks, private scales, and model state stay with the client. The preparation and inference services both hold the public transformer body. Preparation receives stage seeds before inference starts. Inference receives prepared corrections and masked integer tensors later. This path assumes that both services follow the protocol and do not collude. If you run preparation yourself, that trust stays within your own boundary. Two services controlled by the same operator do not provide meaningful non-collusion. Authentication and replay controls protect the transport, but they do not protect against every malicious participant. Timing, traffic volume, public model identity, tensor shapes, and approximate sequence length may remain visible. Use assurance records to evaluate a specific privacy claim. Do not infer privacy from the number or names of the services alone.

title: Reading research and evidence
description: Learn how PLLM connects papers, clean-room implementations, measurements, and publication claims.
text: PLLM records each step from a paper to a published result. It keeps the original source, clean-room method, component version, plan history, benchmark evidence, assurance evidence, and proposed claim separate. Citing a paper does not mean it was reproduced. Passing a unit test does not mean a complete model is supported. A benchmark does not prove privacy. Compare results only when the model, model-body fingerprint, plan, numeric policy, workload, environment, cold or warm mode, and metric definitions match. Keep limitations and failed attempts in the record. Missing evidence is not a pass. Continue with research, benchmarks, and assurance.

title: Metrics
description: Choose clear performance, resource, quality, and privacy measurements for a PLLM experiment.
text: No single number describes system performance. Report tokens per second, time to first token, per-token latency, peak and retained memory, CPU time and use, online and offline network traffic, disk use, preparation work, and failures. Energy and price require measurements from the stated environment. Define each metric's scope and denominator. Keep prefill separate from decode, client from provider, offline from online, cold from warm, and useful output from attempted work. Record model quality and privacy assurance separately from performance. Telemetry must never include prompts, generated text, token IDs, activations, seeds, masks, or credentials.

title: Gemma 4
description: Variant-parameterized text-decoder lowering for exact Gemma 4 E2B and E4B configurations.
text: The Gemma 4 adapter validates exact outer text-decoder contracts for: Adapter Repository revision Raw configuration SHA-256 --- --- --- pllm.gemma4e2btext.v1 google/gemma-4-E2B-it@3e22461f65e89153144f8adb70e3b8c2cc9845a7 1b28f3d2c3100f6c594754b81107428bd7b822a7f48272ca681dae9d2ec38330 pllm.gemma4e4btext.v1 google/gemma-4-E4B-it@ee0ef6023621cff504d758262d4e04895a5af4a2 33b10c02df3c2e8536cf323d29d53262aaa2f4d11dbe19bc729373fbe90295d4 Both plans preserve alternating local/global attention, two head widths, Q/K normalization, PLE, shared-KV suffix state, GeLU-tanh branches, branch-output normalization, and final softcap. E2B additionally doubles effective MLP width in its shared suffix. Variant dimensions and layer schedules are data-driven; compiler paths remain model-neutral. Python SDK example import json from pathlib import Path from pllm import lowermodel config = json.loads(Path("gemma4-config.json").readtext(encoding="utf-8")) plan = lowermodel(config, batch=1, maxinputtokens=16, maxnewtokens=4) print(plan.todict()["adapter"]) gemma4-config.json must be one of the supported pinned outer configurations. Lowering does not execute weights.

title: Models
description: See which model configurations PLLM can describe and what model support does not yet include.
text: pllm.lowermodel(config, batch=..., maxinputtokens=..., maxnewtokens=...) turns model configuration and workload limits into a ModelPlan. It does not download weights or tokenizers, choose a device, or start a runtime. Each adapter validates a specific architecture and produces the same model-neutral plan format. The plan records operators, layers, weight references, persistent state, workload limits, and source identity. When a new model needs a new operation, PLLM extends the shared vocabulary instead of adding model-specific logic to the compiler. Adapter Validated configuration scope Added semantics --- --- --- pllm.qwen2.v1 dense Qwen2 configuration contract grouped-query attention, rotary position, gated SiLU MLP, KV state pllm.qwen3.v1 dense Qwen3; pinned mini-coder-4b fixture explicit head width, Q/K normalization, bias-free attention pllm.qwen35text.v1 pinned Qwen3.5-4B text decoder hybrid full attention and gated-delta recurrence, convolution and recurrent state pllm.phi4mini.v1 pinned Phi-4-mini-instruct decoder fused QKV, fused gate/up, partial LongRoPE pllm.gemma4e2btext.v1 pinned Gemma 4 E2B text decoder hybrid attention, shared KV suffix, double-wide suffix MLP pllm.gemma4e4btext.v1 pinned Gemma 4 E4B text decoder hybrid attention, shared KV suffix, PLE, softcap Describing a model is not the same as loading its checkpoint or running it privately. Compiler support, output quality, benchmarks, and deployment are also separate. Check current support before choosing a model. Python SDK example import json from pathlib import Path from pllm import lowermodel config = json.loads(Path("model-config.json").readtext(encoding="utf-8")) plan = lowermodel(config, batch=1, maxinputtokens=128, maxnewtokens=32) print(plan.todict()["adapter"]) model-config.json contains a supported Hugging Face configuration. This creates a semantic plan only.

title: Phi-4 mini
description: Fused-projection and LongRoPE semantic lowering for Phi-4-mini-instruct.
text: pllm.phi4mini.v1 recognizes the phi3 remote-code configuration used by microsoft/Phi-4-mini-instruct revision cfbefacb99257ffa30c83adab238a50856ac3083. The raw configuration SHA-256 is ac65d86061d3d0d704ee2511fd0eb8713ef19eb6eedba17c3080a4165d5b933b. The adapter emits fused QKV and gate/up projections as linear operations followed by explicit slices. LongRoPE records original context, short and long factor vectors, scaling ratio, and partial rotary width. The tied output head references the token embedding matrix. The upstream model name and adapter identity are Phi-4 mini even though the checked configuration discriminator is phi3. This page does not claim checkpoint import or runtime execution. Python SDK example import json from pathlib import Path from pllm import lowermodel config = json.loads(Path("phi4-mini-config.json").readtext(encoding="utf-8")) plan = lowermodel(config, batch=1, maxinputtokens=128, maxnewtokens=32) assert plan.todict()["adapter"] == "pllm.phi4mini.v1" phi4-mini-config.json must be the supported pinned configuration. Lowering does not import or execute its checkpoint.

title: Qwen2
description: Dense Qwen2 semantic lowering and its present execution boundary.
text: pllm.qwen2.v1 lowers bounded prefill and decode graphs for dense qwen2 configurations. It records grouped-query attention, rotary positions, QKV bias, bias-free output and MLP projections, gated SiLU, KV-cache transitions, last-token output-head evaluation, greedy selection, and feedback. This adapter is structurally validated rather than bound to one repository revision. Checkpoint loading and complete compiler coverage remain separate. Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct is the current runtime and loopback benchmark target, not evidence that every Qwen2 semantic plan is executable. Python SDK example import json from pathlib import Path from pllm import lowermodel config = json.loads(Path("qwen2-config.json").readtext(encoding="utf-8")) plan = lowermodel(config, batch=1, maxinputtokens=128, maxnewtokens=32) print(plan.todict()["adapter"]) qwen2-config.json contains a supported dense Qwen2 configuration. This creates a semantic plan only.

title: Qwen3 and mini-coder
description: Dense Qwen3 lowering with explicit head width and Q/K normalization.
text: pllm.qwen3.v1 extends dense lowering with explicit headdim, per-head Q/K RMS normalization, and configuration-controlled attention bias. Attention projection width is numattentionheads headdim; it is not assumed equal to hidden width. The checked fixture is ricdomolm/mini-coder-4b revision c87892d046a62415a349a6b3aa244bb630fb7417, raw configuration SHA-256 fdbc9e0615fcb88b2cc37aa2b23fa332b3863068d50092aa6bd1e628fd187c92. This establishes configuration parsing and semantic-plan validation only. Python SDK example import json from pathlib import Path from pllm import lowermodel config = json.loads(Path("qwen3-config.json").readtext(encoding="utf-8")) plan = lowermodel(config, batch=1, maxinputtokens=128, maxnewtokens=32) assert plan.todict()["adapter"] == "pllm.qwen3.v1" qwen3-config.json must satisfy the supported dense Qwen3 contract. This does not execute the model.

title: Qwen3.5
description: Hybrid full-attention and gated-delta semantic lowering for Qwen3.5-4B.
text: pllm.qwen35text.v1 lowers the text decoder in Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B revision 851bf6e806efd8d0a36b00ddf55e13ccb7b8cd0a. The upstream configuration SHA-256 is ddc63e1c717afa86c865bb5e01313d89d72bb53b97ad4a8a03ba8510c0621670; the checked fixture adds one repository newline and is verified against both representations. The plan retains the exact 3:1 linear/full layer schedule. Linear layers represent fused input projection, causal convolution state, Q/K L2 normalization, gated-delta decay and update, recurrent matrix state, and gated RMS normalization. Full-attention layers represent doubled query projection, Q/K normalization, partial multimodal rotary sections, KV state, and output gating. MTP configuration remains identity-bound but outside the base decoder graph. These newly explicit operators currently report missing compiler coverage. Semantic lowering does not claim an executable Qwen3.5 runtime, checkpoint importer, generation quality, or protected recurrent protocol. Python SDK example import json from pathlib import Path from pllm import lowermodel config = json.loads(Path("qwen35-config.json").readtext(encoding="utf-8")) plan = lowermodel(config, batch=1, maxinputtokens=16, maxnewtokens=4) print(plan.coverage().complete) False while required operators are missing. qwen35-config.json must be the supported pinned configuration. The coverage result is not an execution claim.

title: Numerics
description: Understand PLLM's integer arithmetic, quantization, rounding, approximation, and overflow checks.
text: A numeric policy records the number domain, scales, rounding, signed decoding, modulus, wire width, coefficient limits, approximation method, and allowed error. Its digest is part of the executable plan and related evidence. The native matrix core validates dimensions and coefficients, selects a scalar or SIMD kernel at runtime, and uses bounded integer arithmetic. Native execution does not remove quantization error, conversions, protocol messages, or client state. Tests must cover reference arithmetic, boundary values, overflow rejection, and a trusted comparison for each approximation. Token agreement and task quality need separate end-to-end evidence. Python SDK example import numpy as np from pllm import AuthenticatedMPC, TrustedPreprocessor mpc = AuthenticatedMPC(TrustedPreprocessor(modulus=65537, seed=0)) print(mpc.centered(np.array([0, 32768, 65536], dtype=np.int64))) This shows center decoding in the reference arithmetic path; it does not establish full-model numeric fidelity.

title: Operators
description: Learn how PLLM describes model operations independently of model family and runtime.
text: Operators describe what a model does without depending on model-family names or a specific runtime. Plans represent projections, normalization, rotary embeddings, attention, recurrent and convolutional state, nonlinear activation, residuals, selection, and input or output boundaries with explicit shapes and settings. A compiler profile lists the operators it can execute. Unknown or unsupported operations appear in PlanCoverage and stop compilation. PLLM never silently replaces them with plaintext or approximate work. Research methods also use these shared operators instead of relying on model-specific weight names. An operator in a model plan shows only that PLLM can describe it. See compiler for execution support and numerics for integer and approximation requirements. Python SDK example import json from pathlib import Path from pllm import lowermodel config = json.loads(Path("model-config.json").readtext(encoding="utf-8")) plan = lowermodel(config, batch=1, maxinputtokens=128, maxnewtokens=32) operators = {operation["operator"] for operation in plan.prefill["operations"]} print(sorted(operators)) This inspects semantic operators; it does not establish execution coverage.

title: Projection and rotary variants
description: Represent fused projections, tensor slices, head widths, and rotary position rules.
text: A fused checkpoint tensor remains one linear operation followed by semantic slice operations. This preserves storage identity without teaching a compiler model-specific tensor names. Query width, KV width, head count, and head width are independent shape facts. rotaryembedding attributes distinguish ordinary RoPE, partial rotary width, multimodal sections, and LongRoPE short/long factors. A compiler must implement the declared variant or report it missing; it cannot silently substitute ordinary full-width RoPE. Python SDK example import json from pathlib import Path from pllm import lowermodel config = json.loads(Path("model-config.json").readtext(encoding="utf-8")) plan = lowermodel(config, batch=1, maxinputtokens=128, maxnewtokens=32) names = {"linear", "rotaryembedding", "slice"} print([op for op in plan.prefill["operations"] if op["operator"] in names]) This reads plan records only; support still depends on compiler coverage.

title: Stateful recurrence
description: Represent convolution and recurrent state in a hybrid decoder plan.
text: Hybrid decoders declare convolution and recurrent state separately from key/value cache state. causalconvolution consumes prior convolution state while convolutionstateupdate produces the next bounded state. gateddeltarule consumes normalized Q/K, value, decay, beta, and prior recurrent state; gateddeltastateupdate records the corresponding state transition. Separate result and state-transition operations avoid implicit multi-output graph edges. Their shared inputs and attributes bind both records to one semantic update. rmsnormgated, gateddeltadecay, and sigmoid retain the surrounding gating equations. Presence in a validated plan is not implementation coverage. Current compiler profiles fail closed on these operators. Python SDK example import json from pathlib import Path from pllm import lowermodel config = json.loads(Path("qwen35-config.json").readtext(encoding="utf-8")) plan = lowermodel(config, batch=1, maxinputtokens=16, maxnewtokens=4) missing = [row["operator"] for row in plan.coverage().operators if row["level"] == "missing"] print(missing) qwen35-config.json is the supported pinned configuration; this reports unsupported operators without executing them.

title: Pipeline
description: Combine model, privacy protocol, preparation, runtime, and deployment choices in one configuration.
text: A Pipeline records what you intend to run. Profiles provide visible defaults, and component overrides keep their versions. The configuration digest covers normalized values, not live connections or provider state. Creating a pipeline does not run anything. Model lowering, research transforms, compilation, deployment, preparation, and session creation are separate steps. Each step returns a record or a structured error. Run pllm config show examples/pllm.yaml to inspect a configuration without loading a model or runtime. Python SDK example from pllm import Cpu, MaskedLinear, Model, ModelAwareCorrections, Pipeline pipeline = Pipeline.fromprofile( "baseline.maskedlinearcpu", model=Model("Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct"), components={"linear": MaskedLinear(), "preparation": ModelAwareCorrections(), "kernels": Cpu()}, ) print(pipeline.tospec()) This creates public configuration only; it does not start a runtime.

title: Preparation
description: Prepare one-time masked material before a private inference request starts.
text: Preparation components define how one-time material is created, batched, committed, transferred, confirmed, erased, expired, and invalidated. They also identify who owns the material and how much can be stored. Protocol and kernel choices remain separate. For public masked-linear inference, the client sends seed batches to preparation. Preparation computes corrections, and inference stores them in a sealed inventory. The client refills inventory only while idle. A restart or idle timeout discards inventory held in memory. Prepared material is part of the system cost. Benchmarks must state whether preparation and loading are included in cold and warm measurements. Python SDK example from pllm.preparation import ModelAwareCorrections descriptor = ModelAwareCorrections.describe() print(descriptor.lifecyclephase, descriptor.roleeligibility) This inspects preparation metadata; it does not create one-time material.

title: Arithmetic garbling
description: Mixed-modulus labels and projection gates over bounded arithmetic values.
text: Arithmetic garbling represents values with labels per modulus. Free compatible arithmetic can avoid tables; nonlinear projection reconstructs signed values jointly from a coprime residue bundle and emits output labels. Gate material is shape-bound, strictly serialized, and consumed once. Reference exhaustive correctness and tamper rejection establish implementation behavior only. Cryptographic review, compiler activation, complete-model coverage, and deployment assurance are not recorded. Python SDK example from pllm.components import listcomponents available = [item.component for item in listcomponents() if "garbl" in item.component] print(available) No arithmetic-garbling component is currently published through the SDK.

title: Half-gates
description: Boolean AND-gate representation and the obligations surrounding free-XOR circuit execution.
text: Half-gates reduce encrypted table material for Boolean AND gates under compatible label and hash assumptions. A component contract must bind circuit identity, wire labels, correlation assumptions, evaluator material, one-time use, serialization, and output decoding. PLLM documents this category for composition and research mapping. Presence in the taxonomy does not state that a reviewed native implementation or executable profile exists. Python SDK example from pllm.components import listcomponents available = [item.component for item in listcomponents() if "garbl" in item.component] print(available) No half-gate component is currently published through the SDK.

title: Garbling
description: Reference arithmetic and Boolean garbling components with explicit maturity and composition boundaries.
text: Garbling is a family of representations and protocols, not one interchangeable backend. PLLM records arithmetic projection gates, Boolean half-gates, lookup tables, and weighted paths separately because their domains, costs, proofs, and conversion obligations differ. Current clean-room arithmetic work is reference-only and unreviewed. It is excluded from executable compiler profiles until protocol, transport, coverage, and assurance gates pass. See research reproductions. Python SDK example from pllm.components import listcomponents garbling = [item.component for item in listcomponents() if "garbl" in item.component] print(garbling) The empty built-in result represents current unsupported SDK state; it is not an execution fallback.

title: Lookup tables
description: Bounded function tables with explicit domains, indexing, leakage, and material size.
text: A lookup-table component maps a finite encoded domain to an encoded range. Its contract records signed interpretation, table cardinality, invalid indices, material ownership, one-time use, communication, and whether selection is data-oblivious under the stated threat model. Tables are useful for nonlinearities only when domain bounds and total storage remain explicit. Approximation and model-quality evidence belong to the numeric policy, not the table name. Python SDK example from pllm.components import listcomponents available = [item.component for item in listcomponents() if "lookup" in item.component] print(available) No lookup-table component is currently published through the SDK.

title: Weighted path
description: Decision-path representations for bounded piecewise or tree-structured secure evaluation.
text: Weighted paths encode a sequence of predicates and selected contributions rather than a dense table. A component must state path topology, hidden and public structure, comparison semantics, branching leakage, numeric bounds, and worst-case work. This is an extension category, not a shipped support claim. Candidate research enters through source and method records before any compiler profile can select it. Python SDK example from pllm.components import listcomponents available = [item.component for item in listcomponents() if "weighted" in item.component] print(available) No weighted-path component is currently published through the SDK.

title: Protocols
description: See how PLLM defines parties, messages, privacy assumptions, and failure behavior.
text: A protocol defines its parties, offline and online phases, inputs, outputs, messages, authentication, replay behavior, one-time material, visible information, trust assumptions, and failure behavior. Model adapters and deployment policy are separate concerns. Current protocols include masked-linear inference and experimental garbling components. Check execution support, security review, assurance, and deployment status separately. Python SDK example from pllm.components import listcomponents protocols = [item for item in listcomponents() if item.category == "pllm/protocol-method"] print([item.component for item in protocols]) This lists published protocol descriptors; discovery does not start a protocol.

title: Masked linear
description: Prepared public-weight linear inference with seeded one-time masks and committed inventory.
text: The prepared protocol separates client, trusted preparation, and untrusted inference roles. Offline, preparation computes Wr-s from domain-separated client seed batches and pushes committed corrections. Online, inference atomically consumes the ticket matching x-r and returns Wx-s for client reconstruction. Inventory identity binds model, body, stage, weight, shape, quantization, ring, modulus, wire width, and attempt budget. Rows are one-use and burned on reservation failure, cancellation, replay, or early completion. Preparation is idle during online chat. This contract assumes protocol-following non-colluding roles and public body weights. Confidential-weight and shared-state protocols are separate. Python SDK example from pllm.protocols.maskedlinear import MaskedLinear method = MaskedLinear() print(method.tospec()) This creates a configuration reference only; it does not allocate masks or start inference.

title: Research workflows
description: Build, reproduce, compare, and review private-inference research with explicit stop rules.
text: A recipe records exact sources, method and component versions, model and workload limits, environment requirements, steps, expected files, evidence, and failure policy. Listing a recipe never runs it. Recipes support reproducibility without making third-party repositories runtime dependencies. PLLM implements methods independently in Python and Rust. Original artifacts remain sources and comparison material only. Run pllm research recipes list to inspect current records. Recipe execution is not supported because sandboxing, artifact identity, and result records are not yet available together. Use the pages in this section to choose a workflow. Build and reproduction work must stop rather than silently substituting an upstream runtime, weakening the privacy boundary, or presenting unmatched measurements as comparable evidence.

title: Native reference
description: Rust crates, the Python binding, data ownership, threading, and ABI support.
text: pllm-core owns validated integer matrices and native execution. pllm-models owns model-neutral semantic lowering. Research-method crates transform semantic plans. pllm-types owns canonical records; pllm-compiler validates executable plans. pllm-python contains only the PyO3 boundary exposed as pllm.native. The Python binding copies bytes into validated integer buffers, releases the interpreter lock around core work, and returns immutable bytes. Matrices own their validated weights; dimensions and contents cannot mutate through public Rust APIs. An executor owns its persistent Rayon pool. The stable Python ABI starts at 3.11. No third-party native plugin ABI is currently published. Python SDK example from pllm.kernels import Cpu descriptor = Cpu.describe() print(descriptor.distribution, descriptor.requiredhostfeatures) This inspects built-in metadata without loading a third-party plugin.

title: Python reference
description: The installed pllm namespace and its generated public API inventory.
text: python/pllm is the only installed namespace. Public objects are imported on demand so metadata discovery does not load model weights, devices, providers, or runtime state. See the generated pllm package inventory for exact modules, symbols, signatures, and native runtime identities. Python SDK example import pllm print(pllm.version)

title: Representations
description: Understand how PLLM records a value's format, owner, bounds, and encoding.
text: A representation states a value's number domain, shape, memory layout, owner, bounds, encoding, and wire format. PLLM uses representations for quantized tensors, ring elements, additive shares, masked activations, CRT residues, garbled labels, packed prefill matrices, and one-time tickets. Each component lists the representations it accepts and produces. Two components can connect only through a compatible edge or an explicit conversion. Matching tensor shapes are not enough. Wire format versions and ownership changes are part of the plan history. Python SDK example from pllm.protocols.maskedlinear import MaskedLinear record = MaskedLinear.describe().todict() print(record.get("inputrepresentations", "not recorded")) Current built-in descriptor does not record representation fields; absence is not compatibility evidence.

title: Experiments
description: Design reproducible experiments with fixed plans, comparable runs, and recorded failures.
text: Before execution, an experiment records its hypothesis, baseline, changed component, model and workload limits, plan digests, environment, metrics, quality requirements, assurance work, stopping rule, and expected artifacts. Report throughput, latency, memory, CPU, online and offline network traffic, disk, preparation work, quality, and assurance separately. Keep failed and negative results. A publication claim must isolate the contribution from its baseline and identify the method unambiguously. See benchmarks, metrics, and publication assessment.

title: Reimplemented papers
description: Trace published private-inference methods to their independent PLLM components, evidence, and current limitations.
text: This catalog is about published work reimplemented as PLLM components. A source record alone does not qualify. Each entry must link the original paper, PLLM's method record, the component that implements it, and the evidence that establishes its current maturity. MPCache MPCache: MPC-Friendly KV Cache Eviction for Efficient Private Large Language Model Inference inspired PLLM's independent pllm.method.mpcache-structural-adaptation.v1 method. It is exposed as the pllm/kv-cache-eviction component and the KvCacheEviction plan transform. - Source and method records - Component catalog - SDK component usage - Current support status The current component transforms compatible Qwen2 semantic plans. It does not reproduce MPCache's complete three-party protected execution, and its fidelity, benchmark, assurance, and protected-execution statuses remain unchecked. Reading copies and PLLM publications Each source record stores authors, title, primary URL, revision, publication details, license, artifact digests, local paper digest, and acquisition status. Local PDFs under papers/ are private reading copies and are not included in the package or website. PLLM's current paper and whitepaper are separate project publications. A citation gives attribution. It does not prove that PLLM reproduced the method, matched a benchmark, or assessed its security.

title: Evidence and records
description: Keep sources, methods, implementations, plans, evidence, assurance, and claims independently reviewable.
text: PLLM research uses immutable, linked records rather than one undifferentiated success status. A paper can be acquired without being reproduced. A component can be implemented without benchmark parity, protected execution, or assurance. A measurement can be valid without supporting a broad publication claim. Use this section to inspect the record types, evidence rules, comparison metrics, and generated catalog. Every public claim should resolve to the exact source, implementation, plan, workload, environment, result, and limitation that support it.

title: Reproductions
description: Reimplement published methods independently in PLLM's Python and Rust stack.
text: PLLM reproductions begin with public papers and locked source records. Contributors then implement the method independently in PLLM. Upstream repositories can help with attribution and comparison, but PLLM does not build them into the runtime or use them as dependencies. The record reports each step separately: source acquired, reference behavior implemented, primitive fidelity tested, native path implemented, model coverage completed, runtime execution available, benchmark matched, privacy assessed, and limitations reviewed. One summary label must not hide a missing step. Follow the clean-room workflow and agent checklist.

title: Runtime
description: Understand which live state a PLLM runtime owns and how it differs from a reproducible plan.
text: A runtime session owns changing state such as inventory reservations, connections, scheduling, the KV cache, native executors, and cancellation. This state is not part of an immutable configuration or plan digest. The Python binding validates input buffers, releases the Python interpreter lock while Rust runs, and returns immutable bytes. Python coordinates models and protocols. Runtime graph support and checkpoint loading remain separate from model planning. Before execution, the runtime rechecks plan identity, component support, weights, and required assurance records. The CLI does not yet provide generic runtime lifecycle commands. Python SDK example from pllm import PrivacyMode mode = PrivacyMode.parse("public") print(mode.value, mode.protocol) Selecting a privacy declaration does not create a session or prove deployment support.

title: Python SDK
description: Plan models, compose research methods, and use supported PLLM runtimes from Python.
text: PLLM ships one Python package backed by Rust. The public API separates model planning from live runtime state so you can inspect and reproduce a plan without including credentials, masks, sessions, or model weights. Install the package Add the pllm package from PyPI to a uv project: uv add pllm Plan a model pllm.lowermodel accepts model configuration and workload bounds. It returns an immutable semantic ModelPlan; it does not load a checkpoint or start an inference session. import json from pathlib import Path from pllm import lowermodel config = json.loads(Path("model-config.json").readtext(encoding="utf-8")) plan = lowermodel(config, batch=1, maxinputtokens=128, maxnewtokens=32) print(plan.digest) Compose research methods Apply a compatible component to a model plan to create a new plan with a record of the transformation. Compatibility with a semantic plan does not by itself establish compiler, runtime, privacy, quality, or deployment support. Run supported workflows Runtime APIs cover specific public-weight and confidential-weight workflows. Support depends on the model, protocol, operator set, deployment, and threat model. Check current support before choosing a path. Continue - Python API reference lists the installed public objects. - Get started covers installation and the first inspection workflow. - Runtime explains live state and execution boundaries. - Models separates semantic planning from executable support.

title: Search
description: Compare compatible system designs against explicit resource, quality, and assurance limits.
text: Search uses component records and evidence instead of importing provider code. Each candidate combines model coverage, operator support, value formats, conversions, protocols, preparation, kernels, party placement, and numeric policy. You can limit memory, CPU, network traffic, disk use, latency, throughput, quality loss, trust assumptions, and evidence maturity. Tradeoffs remain visible; PLLM does not declare one plan best for every deployment. Finding a candidate is not proof that it works. A selected plan must compile, run in its stated environment, and produce matching benchmark and assurance records. Python SDK example from pllm.components import listcomponents candidates = [item.todict() for item in listcomponents()] print([item["component"] for item in candidates]) This discovers candidate metadata only. No public SDK search executor is currently available.

title: Run the local development benchmark
description: Run the real PLLM roles on one machine and understand what the result does and does not measure.
text: Run the real local client, preparation, and inference roles: pllm dev dashboard --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct --no-open Use --tiny only to test transport with generated weights. The dashboard listens only on the local machine and stores a sanitized local history. It does not emit a canonical benchmark evidence record. A local run does not measure a multi-host or wide-area deployment, model quality, energy use, price, adversarial behavior, or production non-collusion. Continue with benchmarks and metrics before comparing results.
